mainTopic: Which altar items need salt? Why the limbs, and not blood, are compared to the מנחה, and how the ברייתא about wood and blood fits with רבי's view that wood needs salt.
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier debate about why the limbs of a burnt offering, and not blood, are compared to the מנחה for the salt requirement. The גמרא first argues that blood looks like a better match. The answer is that the limbs share more features with the מנחה. Then the גמרא returns to a line in the ברייתא: 'I would think even wood and blood, which are called a קרבן, need salt.' It asks who holds that wood is called a קרבן, and the answer is רבי. But רבי holds that wood does need salt, as another ברייתא proves, and רבא and רב פפא add that for רבי wood even needs קמיצה and other wood to burn on. So the גמרא removes 'wood' from the ברייתא. That fix raises a new question: what does the פסוק's limiting word exclude, if blood is already excluded by 'מעל מנחתך'? The answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Blood should have been included instead
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: blood seems more like the מנחה than the limbs do, so blood should be the one included in the salt requirement.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary! Blood should have been included, since blood makes the offering permitted, just like the מנחה's handful does, and blood becomes disqualified at sunset, just like the מנחה does!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the earlier choice to compare the limbs of the burnt offering to the מנחה. It says blood looks like a better match.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the limbs were included in the salt requirement because of features they share with the מנחה. Here the גמרא lists two features that blood shares with the מנחה. First, blood permits the rest of the offering, just as the קמיצה permits the rest of the מנחה. Second, blood becomes unfit at sunset, just like the מנחה. So which item should be compared to the מנחה?

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary; the opposite is more logical
Something that permits the rest of the offering to be offered or eaten

phrases.english: On the contrary: blood should have been included,
phrases.notes: Included in the rule that things brought on the altar need salt.

phrases.english: since it permits, like it does,
phrases.notes: 'It' means the מנחה. Its handful permits the rest of the flour to be eaten, just as blood permits the animal.

phrases.english: and it becomes disqualified at sunset, like it does!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the comparison from the previous section, where the limbs were included in the salt requirement
steps.kashyaTarget: The choice to include the limbs of the burnt offering, rather than blood, based on similarity to the מנחה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Blood shares two features with the מנחה: it permits the offering, and it becomes unfit at sunset. So blood should be the one compared to the מנחה.

steps.title: The limbs share more features
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the limbs share more features with the מנחה than blood does, so the limbs win.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers in two words. The features shared by the limbs and the מנחה outnumber the ones shared by blood and the מנחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When two items each resemble a source, the גמרא goes with the one that has more points in common. Blood has two shared features, but the limbs have more. So the limbs are included and blood is not.
steps.whatToRemember: When two comparisons compete, the one with more shared features wins. That is why the limbs need salt and blood does not.

phrases.english: Those are more numerous.
phrases.notes: 'Those' means the features the limbs share with the מנחה, which the גמרא listed just before this.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Counting the shared features: more similarities beat fewer
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Blood should be compared to the מנחה because of its two shared features
steps.terutzMaskana: The limbs share more features with the מנחה, so they are the ones included

steps.title: Quoting the ברייתא about wood and blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back and quotes a line from the ברייתא: I would think even wood and blood, which are called a קרבן, need salt.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: I would have understood that even wood and blood, which are called a קרבן, need salt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the ברייתא again so it can examine it. This step is setting up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said that from 'every קרבן of yours you shall offer salt' we might include wood and blood, since they are called a קרבן. It then left them out, because nothing else is brought together with them as a requirement. The גמרא is about to ask whose opinion assumes that wood is called a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have understood (a first guess that will be corrected)

phrases.english: The Master said:
I would have understood that even wood and blood
phrases.notes: That is, would need salt, from the פסוק 'every קרבן of yours you shall offer salt' (ויקרא 2:13).

phrases.english: which are called an offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: שׁוֹמֵעַ אֲנִי אֲפִילּוּ עֵצִים וָדָם שֶׁנִּקְרְאוּ קׇרְבָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by going back to an earlier line of the ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברייתא assumes that wood and blood are called a קרבן, which could have made us think they need salt

steps.title: Who holds that wood is called a קרבן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose opinion says wood counts as a קרבן, and answers that it is רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whom have you heard say that wood is called a קרבן? רבי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which תנא holds that wood is called a קרבן, and immediately answers: רבי (יהודה הנשיא).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא took for granted that wood is called a קרבן. The גמרא wants to know who holds that view, so it can check whether the rest of the ברייתא fits with that person's other opinions.

keyTerms.meaning: Whom have you heard (say this)? A way of naming the author of an opinion

phrases.english: Whom have you heard
who says that wood is called an offering?
Rabbi!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן שָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ דְּאָמַר עֵצִים אִיקְּרוֹ קׇרְבָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks who holds the assumption in the line quoted in step 3
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that wood is called a קרבן

steps.title: But רבי holds that wood needs salt!
steps.stepSummary: Problem: רבי holds that wood actually needs salt, but the ברייתא said wood does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבי, wood certainly needs salt!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a contradiction. If the ברייתא follows רבי, it should not leave wood out of the salt requirement, because רבי says wood needs salt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא concluded that wood does not need salt. But the only one who calls wood a קרבן is רבי, and רבי himself says wood needs salt. So the ברייתא seems to contradict the very opinion it relies on.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it even a question? Meaning: it is obvious

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is arguing with רבי. It is pointing out that the ברייתא, which seems to follow רבי, gives a ruling on salt that goes against רבי.

phrases.english: According to Rabbi, they surely require salt!
phrases.notes: 'They' means the wood. The ברייתא's own view that wood needs no salt doesn't fit רבי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer of step 4 to challenge the ברייתא quoted in step 3
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's conclusion that wood does not need salt
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's assumption that wood is called a קרבן comes from רבי, but רבי holds that wood needs salt

steps.title: The ברייתא proving רבי requires salt on wood
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that wood can be donated as an offering, and that רבי treats it like a מנחה, needing salt and הגשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: 'A קרבן מנחה' teaches that people may donate wood. How much? Two logs. And so the פסוק says: 'And we cast lots for the wood offering.' רבי says: wood is a קרבן מנחה, so it needs salt and needs הגשה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as the source for its claim that רבי requires salt on wood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First the ברייתא learns from the extra word 'קרבן' that wood can be donated, two logs at the least, and supports this with a פסוק in נחמיה. Then רבי goes further and says the donated wood is actually a type of מנחה. That means it needs salt and must be brought to the corner of the altar, just like a מנחה.

keyTerms.meaning: Bringing the מנחה to the southwest corner of the altar

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source showing that for רבי, wood is not just 'called' a קרבן. It is treated as a full מנחה with all its rules.

phrases.english: As it is taught: 'A meal offering' —
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:1. The extra word 'קרבן' is what the ברייתא learns from.

phrases.english: teaches that one may donate wood,
And how much? Two logs,
And so it says:
'And we cast lots for the wood offering,'

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אָמַר: עֵצִים קׇרְבַּן מִנְחָה הֵן,
phrases.english: Rabbi says: wood is a meal offering,
and requires salt, and requires bringing near.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the claim in step 5 that רבי requires salt on wood
steps.raayaObject: That according to רבי, wood needs salt
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי says wood is a קרבן מנחה that needs salt and הגשה

steps.title: רבא: for רבי, wood needs קמיצה
steps.stepSummary: רבא adds that according to רבי, donated wood even needs קמיצה, just like a מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: according to רבי, wood needs קמיצה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא takes רבי's view to its logical end: if wood is a מנחה, then a handful-like portion must be taken from it, just as with a מנחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows how fully רבי treats wood as a מנחה. It isn't only about salt and הגשה. Every מנחה rule applies, including קמיצה. That makes the contradiction with the ברייתא even stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: Removing a handful from the מנחה to burn on the altar

phrases.english: And Rava said: according to the words of Rabbi,
wood requires removal of a handful.
phrases.notes: He means a portion of the wood is taken off and burned separately, like the handful of a מנחה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא: לְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי, עֵצִים טְעוּנִין קְמִיצָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds to step 6, showing how far רבי's view goes
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי, donated wood needs קמיצה like a מנחה

steps.title: רב פפא: for רבי, wood needs other wood
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא adds that according to רבי, the donated wood must be burned on top of other altar wood, like any offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב פפא said: according to רבי, wood needs wood.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא adds one more result of רבי's view: since the wood is itself an offering, it must be placed on other wood to burn, like every offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Offerings are burned on the altar's wood. If the donated wood is a real offering, then it can't be the fuel. It needs its own fuel underneath it. Together with רבא, this confirms that for רבי wood is a complete offering, which sharpens the problem from step 5. The next step answers it.

keyTerms.meaning: Wood needs (other) wood to burn on

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי, donated wood is a full מנחה: it needs salt, הגשה, קמיצה, and other wood beneath it. So the ברייתא that leaves wood out of the salt requirement is hard to explain according to רבי. The next step solves this by removing wood from the ברייתא.

phrases.english: And Rav Pappa said: according to the words of Rabbi,
wood requires wood.
phrases.notes: The donated wood has to be burned on top of other wood, like any offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: לְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי, עֵצִים צְרִיכִין עֵצִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second result of רבי's view, alongside רבא's in step 7
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי, donated wood must be burned on other wood, like any offering

steps.title: Take wood out of the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: To fit the ברייתא with רבי, the גמרא removes 'wood' from the list of things that do not need salt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the problem from step 5 by saying the word 'wood' should be taken out of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 asked how the ברייתא can follow רבי if it says wood needs no salt, while רבי says wood does need salt. The answer: the ברייתא really follows רבי, and 'wood' simply does not belong in its list of exclusions. With wood removed, the ברייתא no longer clashes with רבי's ruling that donated wood is salted like a מנחה.

keyTerms.meaning: Remove from here; take this word out of the text

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying wood stops being a קרבן. It is saying the ברייתא should not list wood as something that skips salt, because for רבי wood does get salt.

phrases.english: Remove wood from here,
phrases.notes: Here means the ברייתא that listed wood as not needing salt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 5, now that steps 6 through 8 showed how strongly רבי treats wood like a מנחה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Text correction: a word is removed from the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא excluded wood from salting, which clashes with רבי.
steps.terutzMaskana: Wood is removed from the ברייתא, so the ברייתא no longer contradicts רבי's view that wood needs salt.

steps.title: Then what does the פסוק exclude?
steps.stepSummary: If wood is no longer excluded, the פסוק's limiting word must exclude something else, but blood is already excluded by another phrase.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, what does the פסוק come to exclude? If it comes to exclude blood, that is already learned from the words 'from upon your מנחה'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges its own fix: once wood is removed, the limiting word in the פסוק seems to have nothing left to exclude.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא learned from the פסוק that some things do not need salt. With wood gone, the only item left is blood, but a later phrase in the same פסוק, 'מעל מנחתך', already excludes blood. So the first limiting word looks extra, and the גמרא asks what it is for.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude; a word in the פסוק that limits the rule
It is derived; we already learn it from
'From upon your מנחה', a phrase that comes later in the salt פסוק

steps.whyThisMatters: The גמרא assumes every word of a פסוק teaches something. Fixing the ברייתא cannot leave a word in the פסוק with no job.

phrases.english: But then, the verse comes to exclude what?
If it is to exclude blood –
that is derived from "from upon your meal offering"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the result of step 9's text fix, which seems to leave the פסוק's exclusion with no purpose.
steps.kashyaTarget: The text fix of step 9 (removing wood from the ברייתא)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Once wood is removed, the limiting word can only exclude blood. But blood is already excluded by 'מעל מנחתך', so the limiting word would be extra.
